approachQuestion.prompt: A device records an operation trace. PUSH(value) places a signed 64-bit integer on a stack. POP(claim) removes the top value and records what the device claims it removed. Audit the trace from the beginning. Return the zero-based index of the first POP that underflows or whose claim differs from the actual top. If every POP is valid, return the maximum stack depth reached; an empty trace returns 0. Example: [PUSH(7), PUSH(4), POP(4), POP(7)] returns 2. [PUSH(7), PUSH(4), POP(7)] returns 2, the index of the mismatching POP.
constraints: The immutable trace has 0 to 200,000 operations.
Each PUSH carries one signed 64-bit integer; each POP carries one claimed signed 64-bit integer.
A POP from an empty stack is the first invalid operation.
The output is either the first invalid zero-based operation index or, when all operations are valid, the maximum depth reached; it fits in a signed 64-bit integer.
The input trace is not auxiliary space; the stack stores fixed-size integer values.

options.text: Process operations once with a stack of pushed values. On POP, reject an empty stack or a claim unequal to the top; otherwise pop. Track the greatest depth after pushes.
options.feedback: This directly models the device: the top value is the only value a POP can remove, and the same pass can maintain the maximum depth.

options.text: Store pushed values in a queue and compare each POP claim with the oldest still-pushed value.
options.feedback: A queue removes the earliest pushed value, while POP removes the latest. [PUSH(7), PUSH(4), POP(4)] is valid for a stack but this method compares 4 with 7 and rejects it.

options.text: Track only the current number of values and the maximum count; treat every POP as valid whenever the count is positive.
options.feedback: Depth alone cannot check the claimed value. [PUSH(7), PUSH(4), POP(7)] never underflows, but the POP claim is wrong because 4 is on top.

options.text: For each POP, replay all preceding operations to reconstruct the stack, check its top, and replay the whole trace to find the maximum depth if no POP fails.
options.feedback: The replay can produce the right result, but reconstructing prior state for each POP repeats work and is far from the single-pass solution. This is an efficiency error, not a claim that the replay returns incorrect stack results.

feedback.reason: The trace is defined by last-in, first-out behavior. Both the value check and maximum depth can be maintained while applying each operation to that state.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Choose the time and auxiliary-space pair for simulate-with-value-stack. Let m be the number of operations. The immutable trace and scalar output are excluded from auxiliary space.
constraints: Each operation is processed at most once before returning or reaching the end.
Each stored integer occupies one word in the unit-cost model; stack operations are constant time.
The stack can contain up to m values. No call-stack recursion is used.

feedback.reason: Each operation causes a constant number of checks and at most one push or pop, so the scan is linear. In the worst case all operations are PUSH, leaving m values in the auxiliary stack. The queue alternative has the same broad storage bound but implements the wrong removal order; replaying prefixes repeats earlier operations instead of retaining the current stack state. The output is one scalar and is excluded from auxiliary space.

methodReveal.title: Apply and audit each operation against the current top
methodReveal.description: Start with an empty stack and maximum depth zero. For PUSH(value), place value on top and update the maximum depth. For POP(claim), first reject an empty stack; otherwise compare claim with the top value and reject a mismatch, then remove the top. Stop at the first invalid POP. If the trace ends without one, return the recorded maximum depth.
